utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please have General Blaskic brought into the courtroom? (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Does everybody hear? Do the interpreters hear? Good afternoon. Good afternoon to Prosecution counsel and to Defence counsel. Good afternoon to the witness. I will give you the floor, but I would first like to remind Defence counsel that it has been a week that we have been hearing General Blaskic's testimony,; therefore, I expect that you will now set the amount of time that you are going to need so that the Prosecution will know how much time it is going to have, and that will allow us to set the schedule for our work. Mr. Harmon, did you wish to make a comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours and counsel, and I raise this issue with counsel. It is only a matter of clarification of an issue that was raised during the cross-examination of Defence witness Martin Bell. During his cross-examination, Your Honours may recall, I showed him two brief video clips from the BBC. The first of those video clips in which Mr. Bell says that the Vance-Owen Plan so far from calming the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That was not a protected testimony, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're talking about the journalist from the BBC?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Who is now a Member of Parliament in Great Britain; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The Exhibit number is 573/1, and in that Mr. Bell said that the Vance-Owen Plan, "so far from calming the conflict, seems to have provoked it as the Croats seized for themselves those parts of Bosnia which they believe the plan awards them. The result is a blood-stained partition of the country." I then went on to ask Mr. Bell about that particular clip, and he said he was unsure of the date of when that particular clip was transmitted. I said to Mr. Bell that I believed it was the 20th of April, and he took issue with me, and I said to him that I would come back with a clarification, and I said to Your Honours and to counsel that I would come back with a clarification, and I now would like to inform the Court that following that issue that was raised by Mr. Bell, I contacted the BBC and was informed by the BBC that the date of the transmission of that particular clip that I have just related to Your Honours was on April 21st, 1993, and that they were uncertain as to when it was actually filmed but said that it very probably had been shot the same day, the 21st of April. So that is what I present to the Court for purposes of clarifying Prosecutor's Exhibit 573/1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. I think everybody has taken note of that, and it will be put into the record, unless there is an objection from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is what we thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. All right, General Blaskic -- but first, Mr. Nobilo, please continue with the examination-in-chief of the accused who is now a witness. I am saying this for the public gallery and anyone in it who may be listening to our hearing today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your permission, I would also just like to offer a clarification regarding my response yesterday when asked by my counsel about the meeting on the 21st of February, 1993, and the issue as to the release of prisoners. My response was that I could not recall at that time. Since then, I have consulted my notes, and I realised that one of the conclusions at that meeting was a confirmation that all imprisoned persons were released on the 21st of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hayman, do you want to take the floor?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Just to say, Mr. President, I noticed that the witness was getting very tired by the end of the session yesterday, and I have asked him about that, and the only thing we would like to do, and I will speak to the administrator of the detention unit about this but I want to alert the Court, is that on trial days, he doesn't get any fresh air at the end of the day. He goes into his cell, and he doesn't have any time outside for any fresh air, which I think may affect sleeping and overall bodily health. So I will speak to the administrator about him possibly getting some fresh air after the trial day is over because we hope that will help him sustain his concentration and mental energy throughout what is going to be a number of additional weeks of testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me turn to my colleagues. I believe that all the Judges agree to your taking that initiative. Yes, it is true that the witness -- I remind you that in the current proceedings he is the accused in the trial -- it is important that he be in the best possible condition in order to explain what he wants to explain about what happened. I could add two things for the benefit of the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: witnesses in this trial, that is, if you need some time to rest, even ten minutes, ten minutes or five minutes, that can be very helpful, there would be no problem, General Blaskic, and the Judges will grant you that time to rest. The second point, let me turn to the Defence -- I don't want to interfere with the Defence strategy -- but, in fact, the witness who experiences these events on a daily basis, hour by hour, wants to provide us with all the details, and I said that perhaps it might be best in general, as is the case in all these trials, one must try to go to what appears to be the most essential. But I can't say anything further. You are the only ones, you and the witness, are the only ones who can decide about that. That's all that I wanted to say to you. Would you like to take the floor again, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Just briefly. We are torn between brevity and sharp focus and the importance of the richness of detail for the Court given the ultimate question for the Court will be: Did the accused act reasonably given the resources he had, the available time he had, and the other competing demands on his time and energy? So the fact that there were many meetings with international organisations and so forth and so on and many other problems to deal with of all types, we think is important, but we are trying to find the right balance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. We are going to hold to what we said to the witness, but I would like to convey the Defence request to the Registrar so that we can see, insofar as possible, perhaps we don't want this to be -- we might make it an exceptional situation and that the organisations, such as the detention unit, should allow the detainee to get some fresh air. I don't think this should be impossible, I don't think so in any case, but I will ask the registrar to speak to Mrs. De Sampayo and the director of the detention unit to see if it is possible to grant that. As regards the rest, it has to do with the Defence strategy, and the Defence has to make its choices, but, General Blaskic, we will say that if you get tired at any point, of course, the Tribunal will grant you either a somewhat longer break or even a break which wasn't scheduled. If you need it, please don't hesitate to tell us that. Right now, you are acting as a witness. You are an accused, but for a specific procedural time, you are a witness. All right. Therefore, I now propose that we not delay this any further and move along with the examination-in-chief by Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We attempted today to really synthesise this next segment, and I hope that we can proceed and come to the point of the 15th of April when the conflict between the Croats and Muslims started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I didn't understand that. I didn't quite understand the interpretation. You tried to make things more synthesised. I thought you said that the testimony of the accused would be finished around the 15th of April. I was a bit worried when I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, what we are going to try to do is we would like to, figuratively speaking, arrive at the 15th of April, 1993, today. Yes, by the end of the day, we would like to reach that point in time. We really attempted to synthesise, so to speak, the material that we wanted to present today, and we, however, slightly fear that any attempt at synthesising would just depart a little bit from the full truth, and we really are attempting to present things as they actually really happened, so this is a balance that we are trying to strike between the full detail and the synthesis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, we will now try to just summarise events starting with January of 1993. At that time, you were still in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sorry. On the 1st of March, you were still in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, it was the 1st of March. I thought we were going to go further back yet. I thought, Oh, we're off to a bad start here. Now, yesterday we were at the 21st of February, and if I understood correctly, all Februarys ordinarily end on the 28th except in leap years, so then we would begin with the 1st of March. All right. Let's start with the 1st of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is correct. Sorry. That was just an honest mistake. I didn't mean to scare you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So on March 1st, you were working on a plan for the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what kind of plan this was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the 1st of March, I was working on a draft for a monthly plan of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. My priority was the tasks of organisation and establishment, and I had already dealt with this task before March, but in March, we expected to implement these establishment documents through seminars and lectures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What other plans did you have and what other tasks did you have, apart from the establishment?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Obviously, the priorities were the security situation and public law and order because, throughout that period, we had a number of incidents involving a lot of refugees who were armed, as well as some other armed groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 2nd March, 1993, you received information from the Kiseljak civilian authorities about the expressed desire of Muslims to move out.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I received summarised information of a meeting of the civilian authorities in Kiseljak where it was pointed out that about 60 per cent of the Bosniak Muslim population of Kiseljak had expressed intention to move out of the territory of Kiseljak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In which direction?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were opting for two things: One was third countries, that is, outside of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the second was to the area under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the position of the civilian authorities? Were they leaning towards approving it or not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The position of the civilian authorities was not to approve such an initiative because they believed that it was a result of the current situation in the territory of the Kiseljak municipality. Another problem was pointed out in this document. This concerned the Bilalovac and Brestovsko local communes because two school buildings were taken over by the BH army, and it moved in its troops, and the municipality was unable to organise school classes there. Also there was a problem of freedom of movement between Bilalovac local commune and downtown Kiseljak, as well as problems with private and so-called social property in Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You met with the representatives of the Bilalovac Croats.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. At the request of the Bilalovac Croats who had been expelled, I met with members of this board, which they had organised, and they asked of me a specific position, that is, they wanted to know when they would be able to go back to their homes in Bilalovac. Then they wanted to know what the HVO was doing to protect their private property in Bilalovac and whether it was possible for them to go and visit their households in case they could not return to Bilalovac, and they also asked me why they could not visit their homes, whereas the Muslims from Bilalovac were still able to acquire supplies in the territory of Kiseljak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, you had a meeting with General Morillon, General Cordy-Simpson, and General Prado. Can you tell us the main points that were discussed during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I sent a letter to the UN headquarters asking to be present at that meeting, and the key topic at the meeting was the assistance and mediation of the UN command in implementation of the agreement which was signed by myself and the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, and the stabilisation of the overall situation in the territory of the Busovaca and Kiseljak municipalities. In this meeting, I referred to the statements of the Bosniak Muslim leadership guaranteeing the full freedom of movement and emphasised that it had been 37 days since the road between the Kiseljak and Busovaca municipalities was totally blocked for all Croats living in this area. I also expressed my fear regarding the ability to control the rising discontent among the refugees, and I gave information to the UN commanders about the losses which we had suffered during this time of the cease-fire. The losses mostly resulted from the sniper activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You also received a request for assistance from a Muslim battalion.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The battalion, which was stationed in the area of Koscan over here (indicating), called me on the telephone, their commander called me on the telephone and said that the army of the Republika Srpska is shelling from its artillery pieces their positions, and he asked for assistance, and he received assistance from the HVO within the limits which we were able to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You were also called because you were told that the Croats were shelled by the TO.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The Croats in Zagorice called me and asked me to help them because they were attacked by the BH army members. We assumed that this was the 302nd Brigade because the villages were unable to identify the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next day on the 3rd of March, 1993, you were transported by UNPROFOR to Vitez to a very important meeting. Can you tell me how the trip went and who attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The meeting was very important, and I was transported to this meeting under the same conditions as I was transported to all other meetings. We boarded the armoured vehicles in front of the UN base, and I was brought to the UN base in Vitez. The chief of the European Monitoring Mission chaired this meeting, this was Mr. Thebault, and Colonel Bob Stewart was also the host of the meeting. Representing the 3rd Corps of the BH army was Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic, his deputy, Dzemal Merdan, Serif Kadic, who was an officer with the 3rd Corps staff, as well as Kadir Jusic. Also present was Mr. Jasmin Jaganjac, who at that time was also a counsellor or advisor of Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, who at the time also had the duty of commander in chief of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Zikrija Dzuko was also present. He was the security officer of the joint staff. Also present was a member of the supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina who was also a member of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Franjo Boras. Also present was Franjo Nakic, chief of staff of the Operative Zone, Tomislav Vlajic, and Mr. Saric. The agenda was, the first point, communications, then the barricades/roadblocks, and the return of the equipment and materiel. In this meeting, special emphasis was made on proceeding in the spirit of the agreement signed on the 13th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you just remind us who signed those orders?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those orders were signed by myself and Enver, who was commander of the 3rd Corps. During the discussion, Enver Hadzihasanovic again emphasised that the process of agreement was successful and that there was progress in all areas, but he also claimed that the town of Busovaca was under a blockade and that the town could not be entered, that is, that the Muslims, the citizens of Muslim background, could not enter the town and that the Croats from Busovaca are moving into the homes of Bosniak Muslims in Busovaca. He, that is, Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic, also confirmed the existence of the barricade in Bilalovac and said that the reason for the existence of this barricade was his inability to establish communication with the commander at the barricade and that this was why this barricade was not removed. He also confirmed, in fact, he claimed that the HVO military police had disarmed the whole security detail in the explosives factory in Vitez. Following that, he also requested that the orders of the joint commission be updated and brought further up to date. He also asked that the civilian police take over the control of the checkpoints along the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, did Hadzihasanovic say anything about the causes of the conflict, in other words, the relationship between the politics and the military, including the HVO and the BH army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He repeated the words, I wrote them down, and here I quote them: "Here the army is not the problem; the politics is the problem. We have one territory and a policy of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the one of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." This is what he emphasised in this meeting, and the chief of staff, Franjo Nakic, who was a member of the joint commission together with Dzemo, responded to Enver by saying that the joint commission did go to Busovaca and that it did not find anything about the inability of the Busovaca citizens to enter town. Nakic also pointed out that it was true that the security detail in the explosives factory had been disarmed but that it had not been done by the HVO military police but the Vitezovi special purpose unit military police, and only one shift of the guards in the Vitez explosives factory had been disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us about that guard. What was its ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The ethnic composition of the guard was well-balanced. There was roughly the same number of Bosniak Muslims and Croats, and the workers stood guard. They supplied the security guards from the explosives factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly what Franjo Boras, member of the supreme command and presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, said?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Franjo Boras spoke in favour of having joint action on the part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina against the aggressor. He stressed that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian Defence Council were component parts of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that, this being so, it was to be expected that they should work together and that the incidents and conflicts were the result of the failure of the joint command to function. I supported the position of the commander of the 3rd Corps that all the checkpoints should be taken over by the civilian police, and Colonel Bob Stewart, for his part, laid special emphasis on the fact that it was the duty of all the participants in the meeting to retain and safeguard this peace zone for all the inhabitants living in the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After this particular meeting, you took advantage of the situation and, quite simply, you left the UNPROFOR base. What happened? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the meeting, as a member of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was present, and that was Mr. Franjo Boras, and other high-ranking officials also attended the meeting, I left together with them from the base towards the Hotel Vitez, and I arrived at the hotel, at Hotel Vitez. Probably because of the fact that these high-ranking individuals were present, it was not strictly asked of me to enter the UNPROFOR vehicles and go back that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, on the 3rd of March, 1993, you returned to your headquarters, and can you remind us when you left for Kiseljak, that is, when were you not able to be at your headquarters and to perform the duties of commander at the command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the afternoon of the 23rd of January, 1993, I left the command in Vitez and went to Kiseljak, and I returned on the 3rd of March, 1993, after the meeting in the UN base in Vitez had been concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So on the 4th of March, 1993, your first working day after this lengthy interruption in the headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, what did you do there, first of all, at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in the course of the morning, I had a rather long meeting with the chief of staff, who was Mr. Franjo Nakic, who informed me in detail of all the important events that had taken place during my absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did you have occasion, in the course of February and the end of January, until your return, with Nakic or with any other officer from your command, did you have occasion to talk to them without the presence of a representative of the BH army or the International Community?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not. I saw Nakic only at a joint meeting attended by members of the International Community and representatives of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the other individuals who took part in these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So within the framework of that course of information, were you informed when the most critical points in Busovaca took place, what happened in Vitez, and so on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I learnt of the fact that the situation was most critical in Busovaca on the 28th of January, 1993, when an all-out effort -- an attack was stopped which was launched by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened to the Vitez municipality? Did it participate in those conflicts or making up part of the troops or in any way?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The commander, the chief of staff, told me that they had succeeded in safeguarding the area and keeping it a safe and neutral area with respect to the events that were taking place in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that particular day, did you set up communications with your superiors?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day, I called the chief of staff of the Croatian Defence Council, and I informed him of the military situation in the Operative Zone with special reference to the basic problem of the existence of enclaves and the difficulties in commanding the enclaves. I enumerated for him some of the basic problems that existed which were linked to the question of supplies, coordination, and the HVO activities in general in the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that same day, at 10.00, you convened the commanders of the brigades from the Lasva River Valley. Can you tell us the agenda?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The name was General Petkovic, the one who was the chief of the HVO headquarters? It wasn't Prkacin, it was Petkovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, General Petkovic. I talked to General Petkovic on the phone, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it is 10.00, you had a meeting with the commanders of the brigades from the Lasva River Valley. Can you tell us the agenda, the reason for which the meeting was convened on this first day when you returned?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, during my long absence -- my long absence was one of the reasons for which we decided to convene a meeting as well as the newly arisen situation, the situation that we found ourselves in. The fundamental problem was how to function under prevailing conditions where we had enclaves and certain areas which had been cut off. The agenda for the meeting was control and command. Then we discussed training and drills, the fight against crime, and information about armed groups of criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you began the process of transforming the armed villagers into an army. This process started in December 1992, and you continued this process in the first half of January 1993. During your absence, was anything done along the lines of this process that you started, that is to say, the process of actually creating an army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nothing had been done during that time because I was in Kiseljak, whereas the chief of staff, from the 11th of February onwards, would attend meetings of the various joint commissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The brigades would report to you. Let us now talk about the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade of Novi Travnik which encompassed the potential soldiers from Vitez and Novi Travnik. What did they tell you as the basic problems that they were facing in their particular region?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they highlighted two problems: One was the question of the relationship between the civilian and military authorities in those two municipalities; and, second, the very low power the commanders had of actually commanding and controlling the units under them and where the commanders of the brigade stressed that the commanders were, in fact, the loudspeakers of individual armed villages, that they echoed their views.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, where was the problem in Vitez and Novi Travnik in the conflicts between the civilian and military authorities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The problem was with regard to the fact that the Vitez authorities, as did the civilian authorities of Novi Travnik, they both considered that they should have their own brigade and that the municipality did not wish logistically to supply the Novi Travnik Brigade. Next, there were difficulties with respect to the selection of commanders and choice of commander because there too it was the attitude and position of the civilian authorities that was overriding.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In addition to the problem over authority linked to the civilian authorities in Vitez, what was the situation like in Busovaca? What was the main problem there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Busovaca, the fundamental problem was the fact that the front line, the new front line established vis-à-vis the BH army, was in the Busovaca municipality, and it was approximately 40 kilometres long, and the Busovaca recruits from the ranks of the HVO still had to be engaged on the Travnik battlefront in the Paklarevo sector facing the Serbian army. They raised the problem of not having sufficient manpower to cover such an extensive front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you enumerate briefly what tasks you assigned to the brigades at that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The tasks that I assigned at that first meeting, once I had returned, was to lower tensions with regard to the BH army, to lower tensions, first of all, and to solve problems through a joint commission and to set up commissions for incidents that were formed at a local level, that they should become active in subduing conflicts. I next stressed the need for coordination with the civilian authorities in the municipalities but that the commanders should not follow the orders given them by civilian authorities but that they should implement my own orders, that is, from the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. I asked that competencies be divided and differentiated and that the civilian authorities should deal with civilian matters. Next, a list of weapons and military equipment with the recruits should be drawn up, that was the next task, to make an inventory, and to establish the amount of ammunition that the soldiers disposed of, and to see that the agreements that had been signed up until then with the 3rd Corps of the BH army were translated into practice. I emphasised at that meeting to the HVO that the conflicts with the BH army were not something that we needed and that everything should be undertaken in order to transcend this situation and the difficulties that had arisen but that this should be done through agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, at 3.20 p.m., Mr. Thebault arrived, and can you tell us what you discussed, briefly?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The head of the European Monitoring Mission, Mr. Thebault, visited me on that day in my office at the Hotel Vitez, and I informed him of the topical military situation in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia of the Croatian Defence Council. He asked me to explain to him certain issues which I took to be of a political nature, and I said that I was not competent to discuss that type of question. I emphasised in this regard in particular the subject of the non-existence of firm subordination and relationships between commanding officers and their subordinates, and I said that in the HVO, there were no ranks in ranking commanders and the commanding officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did Thebault say anything with regard to the conduct of the municipalities, for example, the municipality of Vares? Did he tell you what he had noted with the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: What he noted vis-à-vis the civilian authorities, particularly in the municipality of Vares, I was informed of them, he told me of them, and he stressed that the mayor of Vares was behaving and that his conduct was such as if he was building up a state within his own town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the following day, you received an important assessment by the intelligence service of the HVO. Can you tell us the basic thesis from that intelligence assessment? This was on the 5th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 5th of March, I was given assessment by the military intelligence service of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia in which it was stated that fresh attacks were expected by the BH army on Vitez, and that, in the course of that attack, that Travnik would be attacked too so as to ensure a link by road between Zenica and Travnik along with a previous neutralisation of the HVO of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that same day, you were taken up with your struggle against crime. Can you tell us of the orders you issued and what measures you said were to be undertaken?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that same day, I considered that we should go public more and use the local media and publicly to distance ourselves from the criminals and that we should condemn this kind of conduct and that we should clearly state the names and surnames of the perpetrators of criminal acts, that this should be done publicly. I particularly looked into the question of being more efficient and speedy in our action because crime was on the rise in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was there any mention of the arms, the weapons being used by those criminals, the quality of those weapons, what they had and what could be done in that regard?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That was a separate issue and perhaps the most difficult one to resolve because the criminals had anti-aircraft guns, 20-millimetre anti-aircraft guns, and had the whole range of infantry weaponry which could be found in the region. It was my idea that if we were unable to have a frontal conflict with these criminal groups and a frontal settling of accounts with them that we should then make an inventory of them, make lists of them, and then, in cooperation with the municipal defence offices and departments, that we should take the weapons that had been issued and that we should give new combat schedules to them and distribute those recruits and give them different assignments -- give them an assignment. In a situation of that kind, if they were to retain their weapons, then that would be unlawful possession of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 8th of March, there was an incident in Kiseljak, an important incident, with criminals. Just a brief survey of that, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Kiseljak, there was unrest which broke out, there was shooting from automatic rifles in town, there were riots and unrest and there was looting of barracks by criminals, and law and order was generally being disturbed in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 8th of March, there was another discussion as to free passage from Bilalovac to Kiseljak; what was that all about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received reports that up until then, on several occasions, a municipal commission of the Kiseljak municipality and civilian authorities were sent back from the barricade at Bilalovac and that it was prevented from entering the Bilalovac local community from that point. It was demanded, requested, that I make my position clear with regard to freedom of movement and passage because at that time the Bosniak Muslims from Bilalovac moved along the Kiseljak area and the town of Kiseljak. I said that it was my view, in keeping with the signed agreement on the freedom of movement, that my views were in line with that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, you launched an operation to save Mr. Behtic's family. Mr. Behtic was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. At his request, when he told me that his wife was ill and that his daughter was ill, I called the commander of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Dobrinja, his name was Cabir Denas, and asked him to mediate in the evacuation of the Behtic family from Sarajevo to Kiseljak. His wife was seriously ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened with the security, the safety of Muslims during the January conflict?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In March, we continued to ensure the safety and security of families and property in Kiseljak owned by the Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 9th of March, you had something to do with the court in Kiseljak. What was that about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In view of the rising crime rate and the breakdown of law and order generally, I informed myself as to which court in the Kiseljak municipality was functioning at all, and I was informed on the 9th of March, 1993, that none of the courts were working in the Kiseljak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That day is also significant because Mario Cerkez was appointed commander of the future brigade in Vitez. Could you clarify that appointment for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I sent a request to the civilian authorities in Vitez, to the mayor of Vitez, to let me know what their position was with respect to the new -- that is, the first commander of the Vitez Brigade, and they gave their position saying that Mario Cerkez should be the commander of this brigade, this was their position, and they also stressed that this brigade should be established in the Vitez municipality, and they wanted it to be named the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That day you met with the HVO representatives in Zenica. Could you tell us who came to the meeting and what did they ask?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was Mr. Totic and Mr. Baresic, both from Zenica. They asked to be received by me because they were concerned by the accelerated growth of the 7th Muslim Brigade which paraded in the city of Zenica almost every day. They also were saying things which disturbed the Croatian citizens in Zenica. They said that this brigade had been established on the basis of religion, that all members of this brigade were brothers in faith, that there was an increase in break-ins into Croatian homes in Zenica, that some Croatian families were even expelled from their homes, and that they were selling their properties openly in markets in Zenica, and Mr. Baresic said that the BH army intended to violate the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did he mean by that, that the BH army intended to violate the Vance-Owen Plan? In what way, by negotiating abroad, through the media, or in what manner?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was my question to him too. First of all, where did he get this information that the BH army intended to violate this agreement? Then he explained that for a number of years he had worked in the district command of the BH army in Zenica as Dzemo Merdan's deputy and that he had a number of friends with whom he had been talking, and so he came to believe that new incidents would be created, that the agreement between the Operative Zone and the 3rd Corps would be blocked and that most likely a new conflict would be created.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What would be the purpose of these incidents and conflicts with respect to the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The purpose of these incidents with respect to the Vance-Owen Plan would be to show that there was no possibility of implementing this plan in Central Bosnia, that is, between Bosniak Muslims and Croats, that is, the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What instructions did you give to Baresic and Totic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I emphasised to them that the priority was the continuation of fighting on the front lines against the Serbs in defence of Travnik where some of the HVO troops in Zenica were deployed and that, as far as the relations with the 3rd Corps in Zenica, they should respect the spirit of the agreement which we had reached which was the common defence and alliance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next day, on the 10th of March, you received some information from Skradno. Could you briefly tell us what it was and what you did?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The information from Skradno was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. Mr. President, if I may, if the witness is reading a particular matter and that's the subject of the testimony, certainly I would ask that the Prosecution and the Court be given this. I was led to believe and I think the Court was led to believe at the outset that this would be a matter of refreshing one's recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. The Defence maintains that this was a matter of recollection, and I have been watching for some days, as the Court has, where it's taken on, I think, a different form than that and now appears to be an outline with which the witness is testifying from and reading from. The Prosecution has no objection to that methodology if we have a copy of it, as the Court should have a copy of it, and that's my concern at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission, the witness is testifying on events over a period of two years, perhaps several tens of thousands of incidents and events. He has to have an aide-memoire on times and places. I did not notice that he's reading. I think that he just glances at it so that he would refresh his memory, but it would not be possible to have this kind of testimony without any kind of aide-memoire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The witness is under oath. We can ask him. Mr. Blaskic, are you reading a document you've drafted or are they simply notes? After hearing your answer, I'll confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is my personal aide-memoire for this testimony, and my general notes, I didn't even bring with me here. They are in my bag. What I mean is my statement. I do not read here from this. I just glance at it to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'd like to consult with my colleagues on this point. The Judges believe that for the accused, who is a witness and who is giving complicated, complex testimony, he's referring to distant events and that it's the Defence's right in order to refer to his personal notes. In the second place, the Judges have the impression that the witness, who has an excellent memory, ordinarily is not reading but referring to his memory. Thirdly, the Judges do not accept the Prosecutor's objection and simply remind the witness what is customary law in all legal systems, that is, you cannot draft a statement in the detention unit with your counsel and then read it, so a sort of remote control between counsel and yourself. Were that to be the case, it would not be a really fair discussion, but the Judges do recognise that you're referring to complex and distant events, and as an accused, that gives you the right to refer to those documents. I think, having said that, this would be the time to give the witness some time to take a break, and we will take 20 minutes now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume now. The break was a little bit longer than usual. Do you feel a bit rested now, General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before the break, we talked about the event in Skradno on 10 March, 1993. Could you just briefly explain what happened?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received information that six uniformed persons wearing masks were persecuting or driving Muslims out of their homes. I asked of the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade to conduct an investigation and to take appropriate steps against the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 11th of March, 1993, you had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Where is Skradno? What municipality is it in?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In Busovaca, in the Busovaca municipality. The witness could show it on the map for your orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Colonel, why don't you show it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If it's in the municipality of Busovaca, then it doesn't matter. I just didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Colonel, the next day on the 11th of March, 1993, you had a meeting with brigade commanders. Could you tell us what the meeting was about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a meeting on 11 March, '93 with brigade commanders, and the topics discussed were the situation at the front against the army of the Republika Srpska, the drafting of a plan of deployment of troops, then it was the organisational plans, and one of the issues was the issue of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 12 March, 1993, customs within the country, not on the borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina, came into focus. Can you tell us what this was about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That day, I received Ivo Lozancic from Zepce, we had a meeting, and he informed me that for Croats in Zepce and Usora, customs were asked for at the checkpoint in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you point to this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell us where the checkpoint was set up and which Croats were asked to pay custom duties?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The checkpoint was set up at the main road from Zenica to Doboj, and custom duties were imposed on Croats of Zepce and Usora. In fact, they had to pay 30 per cent of the total value of goods which they transported to either Zepce or Usora, so each convoy had to pay 30 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For whom were these goods meant?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was for --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you said --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- it was for the members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is not entirely clear. Who had to pay custom duties and who was this money going to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The custom duties were to be paid by Croats in Zepce and Usora, and the income from this money was going to the fund of the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did Lozancic propose to do something to counter this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that same day, he suggested that he be allowed to set up an HVO custom post at the entrance of Zepce and to have the Muslims of Zepce, Zavidovici, Tesanj, and Maglaj pay similar custom duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you allow him this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not permit him this, and he did not set up such a customs post after this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's move on. On the 16th of March, you had a coordinating meeting in order to come up with measures to fight crime. Who attended the meeting and what were the decisions?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was a meeting which was attended by the president of the district military court in Travnik, the chief prosecutor of the district court, the military police commander, the chief of police administration in Travnik, this is the civilian police authority, and we talked about the operations plan for crime fighting. The conclusions of this meeting were that the military commanders should identify the perpetrators of criminal acts among the military personnel, that the military and the civilian police coordinate their activities against the criminal groups, that is, criminal gangs, that those military recruits be disarmed and reassigned to duties which would enable us to take away the weapons issued to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that same day, several incidents happened in Nezirovici, Donja Veceriska, and downtown Vitez. Can you tell us what each of these incidents were?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Nezirovici, Croatian homes continued to be torched.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Nezirovici is?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nezirovici is in Kacuni local commune in the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Under whose control was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was under the control of the BH army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened in Donja Veceriska, in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was informed that in Donja Veceriska several explosive devices were thrown in front of Croatian homes, three or four Croatian homes, at Haskici, and in Vitez, in the centre of town, a defensive hand grenade was thrown, and a woman was seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 17 March, 1993, you had two meetings. One was with the information officer and one had to do with the Bektic family of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was informed that the Bektic family, who was a Bosniak Muslim family from Sarajevo, had been evacuated to Kiseljak. On that day, there was also a meeting held with the assistant for information, and the building of morale was discussed and the distancing from those who committed criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what was your assessment at that time? Where were the most honest people?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We concluded that the most honest military recruits were those who were deployed along the 80 kilometres of front lines against the Serbs and that they were the ones who really carried out their duties to the highest degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The civilian authorities in Vitez, they also decided to join the fight against crime. What information did you receive from them on that day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The local government in Vitez had decided to establish a special civilian police unit to fight crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day at 1415 hours, you held a meeting with the representatives of the Red Cross, the lady whose name you already mentioned, Iris, and a gentleman whose name was Gianluca. Could you just briefly say what was discussed in this meeting between you and the Red Cross representatives?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The discussion was about the freedom of movement in the area of Busovaca municipality, and we discussed the issue of the Bosniak Muslims under the conditions which were prevailing which meant instability, not being able to freely leave the Busovaca municipality territory. I told Madam Iris that if permission were given in the situation which currently prevailed between the 3rd Corps and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, all Bosniak Muslims would leave the Busovaca area and move to the areas under the control of the BH army and vice versa, that all Croats would leave their areas and move to the areas controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown Defence Exhibit D211, your order of 17 March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After all the discussions that you mentioned, on the 17th of March, 1993 at 1200 hours, you issued an order and it was to prevent destructive conduct. You sent it to the attention of the commanders of HVO brigades, the independent units, the Vitezovi Special Task Force, the Vitez Military Police, and the representatives of the HVO, and you say: "In order to prevent the recurring openly destructive conduct of individuals in HVO uniforms and the HVO armed formations insignia and raise combat readiness, I hereby issue the following Order: 1. Immediately order platoon, company and battalion commanders at all levels to assess the conduct of conscripts and name the persons inclined toward destructive and criminal conduct, in particular. Responsible: brigade commander Deadline: 29 March 1993 2. Identify the causes and consequences of the conduct disruptive to order and discipline in a unit or command for each conscript prone to disruptive conduct in the unit or command. 3. Persons prone to disruptive conduct shall return their weapons, uniform and other and strike them from the lists of the HVO, and to determine appropriate wartime assignment according to the Decree. 4. Should a member of an armed HVO formation decline to surrender to the competent military authorities their weapons, the competent military police shall arrest them and disarm them ..." There is a part which is illegible there, the last sentence. " ... and disciplinary and other measures shall be taken against him. Commanders at all levels shall be responsible for covering conscripts prone to disruptive and criminal conduct in particular who have been recorded as such in the records of platoon, company, etc." The order comes into effect immediately, and it is signed by the Commander, Tihomir Blaskic. Could you tell us, first of all, whether the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may interrupt for a moment? Mr. President, this is just a matter of order, and I don't question for one moment counsel's reading of paragraph 3, but when this was translated in the English version, and I'm not sure if it's true in the French version, Mr. President, it's incomplete. If you take a look at it, Counsel, on number 3 in the English? If I could just ask the registrar to send that back to translation and that the number 3 in the English version comport with the translation as provided by counsel. I don't know, maybe the translation section had an illegible copy when they were doing the translation. Nevertheless, I think that counsel will agree that there is some -- we can add some substance to that paragraph 3. It's just a point of order, and I'm sorry to interrupt counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I think that that's a valid objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, quite possibly. Perhaps I could read out point 3 again and perhaps you could make a note of it in hand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ask the registrar -- I think Mr. Kehoe was not contesting your reading or the translation from the interpretation booths, he simply wants this to be translated officially. However, re-read it, and then we'll ask Mr. Dubuisson to have this translation redone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. That will be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Re-read it, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Once again, point 3, which has not been translated fully, and I read: "3. Persons prone to disruptive conduct shall return their weapons, uniform and other equipment, and shall be struck from the record or inventory of the armed formations of the HVO while, in cooperation with the defence department, adequate wartime assignments should be determined -- an appropriate wartime assignment, according to the Defence." That's what the order states.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now I have my first question related to the third point. What does "appropriate wartime assignment" mean? When you wrote the order on this point 3, you spoke about "appropriate wartime assignment." What was that? What was that assignment?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the assignment, work assignment or duty, because there were two duties: one was military duty and the other was labour, a labour assignment, work assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was the purpose of that to separate criminals from weapons?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that was precisely what we wanted to do because the force of these groups was such that this was the only measure possible at the time to divide the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The second question: Did this order emanate from the meeting that you described some ten minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My third question linked to this document: From the text of the order, we can see that you are issuing this command to the commanders of the battalions, companies, platoons, and so on and so forth; and in reading the beginning of this document where we can see who it is addressed to, it would appear that the order was sent to the civilian authorities and the civilian police and the military police and the Vitezovi and so on and so forth, as is stated in the document, top of the document. So could you explain this? Who are you issuing this order to and who are you sending it to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it is stated here to the presidents of the HVO -- the representatives of the HVO, and I'm informing all those who are not immediately subordinate to me, I am informing them of what the military sector would be undertaking, and at the meeting with the representatives of the Justice Department, civilian police, and military police, in fact we agreed that everyone from his area of responsibility, in order to fight crime, should undertake certain measures and certain action, each within his realm. Point 1 states who the order refers to and at what command levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, to make things clearer, with this order, are you ordering the civilian police to do something or the military police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The chief of the police headquarters of Travnik, the civilian police, I am informing them what the command will undertake, that is to say, the command, the headquarters of the Operative Zone, after the joint meeting that was held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I am going back to -- I agree with the question that was asked, but it was an order, was it not? You were giving an order, were you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was giving an order which was sent to some addressees, to their attention, to the attention of the addressees, and to some for this order to be carried out. So for all those immediately subordinate to myself ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Two more questions on this subject to make it completely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, look at point 1. Who was responsible to you for the implementation of this order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You can clearly see that it is the commanders of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What is the deadline?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The deadline was the 29th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Look at point 4. Who is responsible to you in point 4 for implementing the order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The commanders of the battalions, the commanders of the companies, and the commanders of the platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are they all individuals who are subordinate to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they are all individuals in the structure, organisational structure, of the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, subordinate to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you make any individual responsible from the civilian authorities, the police, civil police and so on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I merely informed them of what I was undertaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, any of the six points from the order that you drafted, did you make responsible for the implementation of those six points anybody of the civilian structures?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed. On the 18th of March, you received from your security assistant information about two serious crimes that had been committed; two killings, in fact. What were they about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received information about an investigation that was going on with regard to the killing of Elezovic and Sehovic, and a report from the security authorities was that individuals had been discovered -- the perpetrators who had taken them away had been uncovered and who had killed the two individuals, and that the whole case had been sent to the military district court in Travnik and that proceedings were being taken there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it ascertained who took them out from Kaonik camp to do trench-digging?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My security assistant informed me that this was done by individuals with a name and surname who were thought to be suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next document, please, D358.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 18th of March, 1993, you wrote the following order, and you had the order dispatched to the representatives of the European Monitoring Mission. On the upper right-hand corner, you usually say to whose attention the order is, so we have the European Monitoring Mission representative Zenica, then the HVO Croatian Defence Council brigade commanders, commanders of independent units, commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion, and Chief of the Police Department, Travnik. The title is "Ensuring the unobstructed movement of representatives of the European Monitoring Mission." "Order. On the basis of previously signed agreements on the unobstructed movement of vehicles carrying representatives of the European Monitoring Mission, with a view to ensuring full compliance and proper procedure, I hereby order: 1. That the unobstructed passage of representatives of the European Monitoring Mission be ensured on all roads in the zone of responsibility of the Units of the HVO, the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. 2. That the personnel manning the checkpoints: (a) establish and take note of the signs on the motor vehicles of the monitoring mission without halting the motor vehicles; (b) approve passage of motor vehicles carrying monitors without halting them at checkpoints. 3. Subordinate commanders shall be personally responsible to me for carrying out this task. They shall brief commanders subordinated to them accordingly and confirm receipt of the Order with their signature on the reverse of the Order. 4. This Order shall come into force forthwith." It is signed Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. I should now like to ask you the following: On the right-hand side, you wrote that you are sending the order to the attention of the European Monitoring Mission representatives in Zenica. Were you in command perhaps of the European Monitoring Mission? Are they subordinate to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. But the topic of the meeting was, on the 3rd of March, 1993, in Vitez, between, amongst others, the -- and we discussed the checkpoints, among others. I drafted this order precisely with the intention of informing the European Monitoring Mission of the rights and unobstructed movement on the communication lines under HVO control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So let us clarify once and for all your method of work with regard to all your other orders because this is a good example. When you write on the right-hand side who you are sending the order to the attention of, do you also enumerate both those who are subordinate to you and those to whom you are sending the order for attention?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The order in correspondence is usually sent to the attention of certain individuals or institutions, to inform them, and others for the order to be implemented, executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where can we see, in this particular order, who you are ordering? Who is duty-bound to implement your order? Where can this be seen in the manner in which you draft your orders?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After every activity, I say who is responsible, the responsible individuals are, and then I state who the responsible individuals are, and sometimes I state the way in which the order must be implemented and the deadline because, unfortunately, I had associates from civilian life, they weren't military professionals and officers or typists.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So in this particular order, point 3, how do you designate who is to implement the order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My subordinate commanders, and I emphasise this here in particular along with a signature, because I say "with their signature on the reverse of the Order," which means that they have been informed of the order so as to eliminate any possibility for voluntariness or self-will at the checkpoint by individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. May we proceed? We move on to 19 March, 1993. In order to fight crime perpetrated by men in uniforms, you took an additional step which may be significant, and you do it together with the logistics people. What was that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked on that day of the assistant for the logistics to create insignia for the members of the HVO so that we could distinguish between the military recruits and criminal gangs. My intention was to have every member of the HVO wear the proper insignia on the arm of his uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 18th of March, in Travnik and Kakanj, there were killings of HVO soldiers and there was an incident involving explosives in Donja Veceriska. Can you explain what happened?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is true that two HVO soldiers were killed in Travnik. The murders were committed by members of the Mujahedeen units, and this created tensions in Travnik, and in Kakanj, an HVO soldier was also killed and the HOS commander from Kakanj, and that also undermined the security situation there. Also, in Donja Veceriska, additional explosive devices were thrown at Croatian homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, you asked for an analysis, that is, a list of the burned houses in Bilalovac and Kacuni. What type of analysis was this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My chief of staff visited the areas of Kiseljak, Busovaca, and Vitez, together with Mr. Dzemo, on an almost daily basis, and they made an inventory of the houses which were destroyed in compliance with the European Monitoring Mission request. I wanted a summary of the results so far of this work of the joint commission: how many structures were burned in the areas of Zenica, Busovaca, and Kiseljak which had been involved in the January conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So what was the essence of your request?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I requested that the information be separated and that the structures which were burned up until the 31st of January, 1993, and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why that date? What would have been the difference?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had signed the agreement on a cease-fire on the 27th of January, 1993, Dzemo and I did, and on the 30th of January, 1993, a meeting took place between members of the joint commission, Dzemo, and Nakic. I believed that the structures burned down on January 31, 1993, were the ones which were burned down during the armed conflict between the 3rd Army Corps and the Operative Zone. After the 31st of January until March would be the structures burned down during this truce and during the period of the implementation of joint orders which were signed by myself and Enver as commanders of the joint command or joint commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you focus on the structures which were destroyed during the fighting or the ones which had been burned after that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not make any objections regarding the structures burnt down by the 31st of January, but I objected to those which were burned following that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, the 19th of March, 1993, you had a meeting in Zenica which was supposed to be attended by the HVO representatives and BH army representatives and European Monitors; however, the BH army representatives did not show up, so you held a meeting with the representatives of the European Monitoring Mission. Can you just briefly describe what happened in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was supposed to be a meeting with representatives of the 3rd Corps, but when I arrived in Zenica for this meeting, the chief of the Monitoring Mission, Thebault, was present, and on the other side, only the representatives of the HVO were present. Mr. Thebault pointed out that the extraordinary events and incidents which had taken place in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps and Central Bosnia Operative Zone are spinning out of control, that it is almost impossible to even register them, let alone respond to them. He especially highlighted the local commanders and problems with implementation of orders, emphasising that the behaviour of local commanders is frequently counter to what the orders which were issued were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me slow you down a little bit to make the record perfectly clear. I want to take you back to the burnt houses which you were listing. Who were the owners of these burnt houses?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The owners were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the other side? Did Dzemo Merdan also point out the problem of burned-down houses owned by Muslims, and if he did, where were those houses?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time he did not, but later on, starting on the 20th of March, I was informed that the joint commission was also trying to identify and list the burnt homes of Muslims in the town of Kiseljak. With respect to damage, Dzemo only asked that the information be broken down by municipality, that they be given separately for Zenica, Kiseljak, and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Outside of the town of Busovaca, was there any mention of any Muslim homes being burned down?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When were those structures burned down, based on information you received in March?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Most of the structures under the control of the BH army were burned down following the 31st of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Muslim structures, did you have such information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For the most part, this was March.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When were the Muslim houses torched, that is what I mean, not when the meeting was, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These structures were burned down during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In which month?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first agreement was signed on the 26th of January, so I believe that the conflict was over by the end of January, that is, the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let me move on. I just skipped over this, but at one point you received a complaint from the International Red Cross that they were not allowed to enter the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade, which is where the prison was, so somewhere around the 23rd of March, you launched an investigation in that respect. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: By investigating this problem of barring the entry in the barracks, I determined that the visit of the Red Cross had not been announced that day, that the gentleman from the Red Cross -- actually, the lady who was visiting asked at the gate to see a representative of the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade who, at that time, was not even present in the barracks, and when the soldier -- excuse me, when the soldier at the gate told her that the brigade commander was not around, so they could not be received by him because he was not there, they went back. I informed, in writing, the representatives of the Red Cross of this event, and I asked of Commander Bozic that in the future the officials be received, regardless of whether the commander was there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean the officials of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and I also said that they were not obliged to announce their visits, in other words, that they had the right to come in and review the premises and visit whenever they want.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 23rd March, 1993, you talked to Totic about the Zenica HOS. Can you tell us just in a few words what he asked of you and what oral order you gave him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He announced a possibility of HOS from Zenica, at the strength of about a battalion, their desire to become part of the HVO. I asked of him to initiate a discussion with the commander of the 314th Brigade of the 3rd Corps --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and that only when he gets approval of the commander of the 314th Brigade of the BH army, we could move on with the procedure of absorbing this unit, however, that this could only be done on an individual basis. In other words, every military conscript with his equipment could become a member of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, why did you want it to be done on an individual basis?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He informed me that within the HOS units, that some of these individuals had previous criminal records and that some had engaged in criminal acts, and at that time, as you can see from the previous orders, we had major problems with criminal elements in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. I was very explicit to Commander Totic and said that we did not need such criminal elements to help us in defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On this same day, the 23rd of March, 1993, at around 1500 hours, you received a European Monitoring Mission official who came, and can you say what Mr. Pedersen had to say about the behaviour of the HVO military police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The European Monitors had the practice that if an official was leaving his post, they would visit the commanders, either myself or Enver, if it was the HVO, it would be me and for the BH army it would be Enver, and Thorping, the outgoing officer, noted that he saw progress and that he saw that the implementation of the joint orders of the joint command was improving, but he pointed out also that it was important that the orders be implemented at all levels, that is, at the level of brigades, battalions, and so on. He was surprised that there were no ranks at the HVO, and he asked, how did we distinguish between different levels of command. I tried to give him the best information I could and told him that the HVO operated on the basis of superiority and subordination but that there were still many problems within the chain of command. After that, Mr. Pedersen gave an example where an HVO unit had taken four Muslim civilians from Vitez prisoner, Beso Pezic, Music, I think they were father and son, Music, those were their names, and the commander of the military police tried to free these arrested civilians in the presence of the European Monitors. He did not succeed in this because the local commander of the military unit did not allow this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would you invite the witness to clarify something which is not quite clear to me?
