There were, he said, no ranks in the HVO, but the HVO operated on a principle of superiority and subordination. How did the commander at the top communicate an order to any branch of the HVO? Presumably, he would have to address his order to an individual. How did he identify that person?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The witness will answer himself.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, command, in some armies, functions according to the principle of rank. The HVO did not have ranks, and everybody was referred to as "commander," so the commander of a squad, that is to say, a group of ten soldiers, he was also a commander, just as a brigade commander was referred to as commander. There was no differentiation between a commander and commanding officer, and command and control functioned on the basis of direct subordination towards a direct superior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, how was the commander of a group within the HVO identified?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was actually the greatest problem within the HVO, Your Honours, because there should have been a structure, to have squads, platoons, brigades, and so on, whereas we had only started to establish them in November 1992, that is to say, from the 25th of November, 1992, when we started this process of formation, and that is why I spoke about commanders of villages, for example. Let us take an example. The village will elect one commander today, and it would be someone else tomorrow, but he is the commander for that particular village, regardless of whether there are 5, 15, 20, or 50 military recruits, so there wasn't a structure below him. In military terms, I would say that the pyramid was reversed. The top was at the bottom and the flat part was at the top. The peak was at the bottom. It was upside down, an upside-down pyramid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This was a really important point, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we're going to take a break. Yes, I think it is a very important question, but in passing, you seem to say that there were armies that were able to operate without any type of ranks. Perhaps you could mention a few of them to us or at least the Defence counsel will do that for us. I think for right now we're going to take a 15-minute break. Did you want to add something, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, nothing, I just suddenly had an idea, the Chinese army, for example, had no rank but it functioned, the witness can tell you more of that, during Mao Tse-tung's rule because, as a relic to the bourgeoisie, they considered ranks to be in China a relic of the bourgeoisie --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Isn't it also true that the Soviet army also had no ranks in the '20s?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, during Lenin's day, it did not. Later on, it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we might all think about the fact that the two armies you're mentioning, despite the absence of ranks, seem to have been able to resolve the questions and problems of criminality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, the President of the Trial Chamber, Judge Jorda, asked you before the break, that is to say, he reminded you that there were armies functioning without rank. Can you tell us briefly how those armies function?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those types of armies function according to the principle of the relationships between subordinate and superior via command posts, positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does that mean in practice?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let me give you an example. In practice, this would mean the position of the commander of a brigade, who has three or four commanders of battalions, then you have the commanders of companies, then the commanders of platoons, going downwards, and commanders of squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does this mean that there is a firm hierarchy depending on a command position and that you know exactly who is superior to whom?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that, in fact, means that there is a well-defined command position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, according to that model, let us say in popular terms it was according to the model of the Chinese army, which is the best known army functioning in that way, that you tried to form your brigades according to that principle in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I used precisely that model and tried, from the 25th of November 1992, to establish and form brigades of the Croatian Defence Council out of an armed people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Although in our chronology of events we haven't arrived at this point, but this is an important point, could you explain to the Trial Chamber, please, what happened with this set-up, the set-up that you were creating, in the April war of 1993? Did the brigade actually come into existence and start functioning in that way?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, that structure which we, that is to say, I, endeavoured to form was alive only on paper, but when we were forced to test its mettle, so to speak, in practice, then this functioning was impossible, and spontaneously the situation reverted back to quite another situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us briefly, what did it revert back to? How was the defence of your enclave in April, May, and June and throughout 1993 organised? What organisational structure did you have instead of a brigade in April, May, June, and so on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The organisational structure was as follows: We had commanders of villages or regions, we had commanders of sectors which included three or four villages, and we had a commander for the entire region, and we called him the brigade commander, that's how we referred to him, because he kept that term, but, in fact, he was the superior to the commanders of these sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: To make matters clear, what you had programmed on paper, that is to say, that the brigade should have three battalions, that battalions should have three companies, and so on down the line, did this function or did it disintegrate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it did not function, it disintegrated, and through my testimony, you'll be able to see this, how and when through the chronology of events.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You had a village commander, the commander of a village. Perhaps he had 100 people under him. Within those 100 individuals, was there a structure within the village from top to bottom?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Every individual there, in actual fact, in 80 per cent of the cases, had a trench in his backyard, so to speak, in front of his family house, and he functioned in such a way that he would defend his hearth and his family and his house, and it was not important what kind of orders were issued and who they were issued by, that was irrelevant. Individuals of this kind were there to defend their territory, their homes, and they thought that they were the ones who were best able to decide on the defence of their own homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What kind of psychological situation did the soldier find himself in, having a trench in his own front yard or backyard and having his wife and children at home? What was his relationship towards order and military discipline in general?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I defined this on one occasion and said that, in the Lasva Valley, I had a multitude of generals and very few soldiers, that's how I defined it, so this was not because it was just the self-will of these peasants, villagers, but they were defending their very lives, so it was a terrible, chaotic situation. I tried to clarify it. Whenever I spoke to anybody, I tried to make them understand, including the European Monitors and everybody else I talked to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One little question, General. You had a structure and you had an hierarchy within the HVO which assisted you in ascertaining who was the commander of any particular group, that's how I understood you, and there was a principle of superiority and subordination at work. I'm still left with this unanswered question in my mind: How did you identify the particular person as being the commander of any particular group? I know of two methods. Maybe there are more than two methods. One is election, you elect a named person to a position, or some superior authority appoints a named person to a position. Now, in either of those ways, you have an appreciation of a particular office holder, John Jones, let's say. How would you know, from the operation or the principles you described, which particular person was the commander of a particular group?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'll try, Your Honours, to take it in order. We did not have a functioning structure, but we wanted to have a structure which would function, we wanted to establish a structure, but I said that I personally worked on mobilisation development. That was a level which the Defence Ministry of each country is in charge of, whereas I was only the operative commander. The road to creating a structure is a much more lengthy one than the one we had, but we wished to have it, we wanted to have it. Of course, as we did not have a structure, we could just have wished for relationships between superiors and subordinates. How we were able to identify the individual to do the commanding, well, the village elected him. I was in the Lepenica local community, for instance. I was invited there as a guest and to listen how they were going to elect a commander for that particular village on that particular day, but looked at from military eyes, he was only a spokesman for the village, in fact, because the problem lay in the fact that every villager or peasant in his own yard had a trench, and he functioned in such a way as to defend his own home and his own family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I understand perfectly from the description you have given of the methods which led to the identification of a village level commander, but as you progressed higher up the pyramid of authority, how did you identify other commanders at positions at which the village electoral system would have ceased, I imagine, to apply?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I tried today to clarify matters by quoting an example. Perhaps I could start off by dealing with the commander of a brigade. The municipal civilian authorities would propose and appoint a commander to that post but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That answers my question. Somebody appoints somebody to a certain position.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but we spoke about the functioning of the chain of command and the power to command or the impotency, the lack of power to command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Blaskic, as far as I know, most of the citizens served either in the JNA or in the Territorial Defence in respect of each of the republics; therefore, for all of these villages, when we speak about these villages, what was the experiences, what were their expectations, what was the background of each of the citizens, that is, these people had some experience of that hierarchy? Could you throw some light on this point, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I shall try, Your Honour. It is one thing when we look at a soldier as an individual and we say that he did his military service, then that is correct, but he was trained in the basics of handling personal weapons. Let me try and be clearer. He knows how to load a weapon, how to target it, and how to shoot. But in peacetime, for the training of a battalion, for example, at least six months are required for the members to be trained properly. For an army, training is one problem, and to drill them to act as a whole is another problem. When we speak about the concept of the JNA and Territorial Defence, then it is quite true, what you said is quite true, but the nucleus of Territorial Defence was composed of the JNA, so there was a professional formation, and the protagonists were mobilisation and the use of that manpower, but the JNA had been trained to defend the country from an external aggressor, whereas we had a new situation here where the conscript was defending his own home and his own family, and that is where the problem lay. The problem was to have this chain of command function properly. On paper, everything was wonderful, but I spoke about the defence of Travnik, sector 1 and sector 2, and the Travnik Brigade was not able to defend it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General Blaskic, the experience which the people had, either in the JNA or the Territorial Defence, would give to them a culture of a hierarchy; is that true or is that not true?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, it did provide the culture of a hierarchy, Your Honour, up until the moment when that recruit found himself in his own yard having dug a trench and starting to defend his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Could one say, in order to go back to Mr. Nobilo's expression regarding the psychological state of mind, could one say that those people had lost the culture of hierarchy because they realised that there was no state or any other type of organisation, or am I wrong in saying that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. It was a chaotic situation, in actual fact, and people had tried, and I will try and be simple in my explanations. Today, for example, is Wednesday. They had a state until Tuesday, for example, with firm control, with a potent apparatus, a powerful apparatus. The next day, the following day, none of that existed; everything had practically fallen apart. There was a collapse, a general collapse, in the functioning of structure. The relationship towards weapons is perhaps another good example in point. Never in the JNA could a soldier have a rifle without having his commanding officer supervise him or any other kind of supervision; whereas in Vitez, they had explosives and arms and military materiel in their own homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So, in conclusion, one could say that the people felt themselves to be totally insecure because of the lack of organisation and each person relied on something or somebody in order to defend himself?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have a question, a very simple one. You had a uniform, did you not? You were a colonel. You had stripes. What kind of stripes did you have? In Western armies, at least in the armies of the country that I know, a colonel has five stripes. How many did you have?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did have a uniform, yes, and I'm sure that every child from the age of seven upwards had a uniform. It was the most popular type of clothing that people wore in the region. That's the first thing. So I did endeavour to have insignia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's not the question I'm asking. I'm asking whether -- you had a uniform, you had stripes, the size of which show that you were Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did have that. I had both a uniform and insignia and a rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What kind of stripes were they? Were they stars or were they stripes? What were they like? We have seen some pictures, but I don't remember very clearly.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I had two sort of stripes and there was a yellow band around it, and the insignia was very visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. All right. So my question is: The one who was your deputy, did he also have a uniform, the one who was below you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No individual had any rank in the Central Bosnia region belonging to the HVO except for myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You said there were no stripes. All right. I would be frustrated to hear, because the sector commanders were not named by the village -- not the villages. How were these sector commanders appointed, the ones who included several villages?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I did that without agreement from the village, I would not be able to implement it in practice, and the commander of a sector had no rank. There were no ranks; they did not exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, I understand. But how could -- one could recognise that at night when it would get dark. Would he be walking around with it written on his uniform? It seems a very complicated system to me. In all the world's armies, I think that even in the Chinese army, there is a uniform with a distinctive sign, either a larger cap or a larger something else. I understand that for the village commander, he would be appointed by the entire village, but when there were several villages, I'm losing you. Go ahead. If you can answer that question, please do, and then we'll move onto something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask the question, and I think that this will make you understand. What you were in command of, was it an army or was it not an army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was not an army, and I informed all the people that I had occasion to meet, it was not an army, it was a classical armed people. We called them the armed peasants or villagers. But I myself wanted to create an army out of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Once again, to jump over time, up until the end of the indictment, did you manage to form an army of some kind in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I think, according to the reports of the MPR that we undertook that we had succeeded in forming an army. Had we had more time, we would have even better organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We'll get to this in the coming days, that is to say, how the army was formed. I would just like to ask one more question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we're going to go on. The accused has to be able to give his testimony. But I take the liberty of calling your attention to the point, which is a fundamental one, when we talk about responsibility, that is, the person responsible, a person has to be able to identify himself officially. Well, all right. If you don't mind, please continue, unless my colleagues have any other questions. But these are questions which allow us to move forward. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we continue, just one additional question in this area. Perhaps it will be of importance. What is the relationship between those who elect a local commander and this commander's responsibility; in other words, to whom is this local commander responsible?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The local commander answers or is responsible to those who had elected him, to his electorate. As I said, it's a reverse pyramid. The local commander reports to those who had elected him. This is why, in my testimony, I said that they were sort of couriers of the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, is it the basis of the chain of command that the subordinate person should report or be responsible to the superior one?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is the basis of commanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If your subordinate is answerable to the village or to the municipality authorities and not to the superiors, can you command this person in the complete sense of the word?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you agree with me, we will move on to the chronological set of events. On 24th March, there was something relative to the military police. You had a discussion with the deputy commander. If you can tell us now, so that we don't have to repeat it every day because now we will encounter this more frequently, what was the situation like in the military police with respect to crime?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Within the military police, there were some perpetrators of criminal acts, in other words, individuals who had previous criminal records, and on several occasions, I insisted that measures against such individuals be taken as part of the reorganisation of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From whom did you request this, and could you carry it out yourself once you identified the problem?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not competent to carry out the implementation of these measures, and I asked the military police commander and his deputy to inform me whether they were able to solve this issue, whether they were prepared to solve it, or whether they had an interest in having this issue solved. This is the issue I raised at the morning briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 24th of March as well as on the 24th of March, you had contacts with respect to providing assistance to the Muslims in Gorazde and, on the 25th, to the defenders of Olovo. Can you tell me, what were your relations with the Muslims who were defending Gorazde and Olovo and how did you assist these defences?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 24th of March, I sent assistance for the defenders of Gorazde, but this had been a continuous type of assistance. It consisted of spare parts, military spare parts, which were needed for military production which then helped the defenders of Gorazde. It mostly meant the ability to produce ammunition. The assistance to Olovo was continuous, and on the 25th of March, when I received information that the state of defence of Olovo was critical, I requested of the Vares authorities to insert its military units in order to help the defenders of Olovo. Until then, we were sending assistance in ordinance and food and everything else we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell what your motive was in assisting the defenders of Gorazde and Olovo?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Gorazde was completely surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: By the Serbs. They were in a very difficult situation in that area. As I said, for a long period of time, we had very good cooperation, and one of my colleagues at the military academy and later on during my career was involved in the defence of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 25th of March, you received information from the intelligence agency about worrisome developments in the territory of Konjic. What was going on there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: During the day, I received information that the BH army, more specifically, the Suad Alic Brigade from Konjic had attacked Croat populated areas of the Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this the same area where there was a conflict in January between the HVO and BH army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. These were the same areas where, in January, there was a conflict; more precisely, on the 12th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 25th of March, you had a regular meeting with the brigade commanders. Do you think that you need to highlight something that took place in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this meeting with the brigade commanders, I asked to be informed -- one of the issues was about the measures which had been taken against the criminal groups in each single brigade. I also asked that they insist on disarming groups of criminals to retrieve their weapons and military equipment. I also asked that all those who were not implementing the agreements signed between the Operative Zone and the 3rd Army Corps in Zenica be removed from the joint commission, and I had in mind the HVO members.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You also had a meeting with Mr. Aleksovski, the warden of the military prison. Can you tell us what happened in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day, I had a meeting with Zlatko Aleksovski, warden of the district military prison, at his request, and he showed me the rules and regulations and decisions which the district military court and the competent ministry had adopted which defined the district military prison as an agency of the district military court. He also asked for assistance from me in logistical supplies; more specifically, he asked for a motor vehicle in which he could take prisoners to the district military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did Aleksovski complain about problems which certain individuals created for him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He complained about the behaviour of the reconnaissance platoon from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade which was stationed in the building adjacent to the district military prison, that is, in its immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did he have any complaints about the military police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he also had certain complaints about the behaviour of individual members of the military police, their treatment of detainees, and also their treatment of the guards at the district military prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I now please have Exhibit D190 be shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, here we have a document dated 25 March 1993. Its heading is "Estimation of Possible Activities by a Potential Aggressor in the Territories of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone," drawn up according to zones, which was delivered to you by the Chief of the Military Intelligence Service for the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. I'm not going to read the whole text but just a couple of lines that refer to Busovaca, and let me take you to the heading -- it's page 2. Bottom of the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think you had it there. There.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The heading is -- subheading is "Area of Busovaca, Vitez, Travnik, and Novi Travnik." I'm reading a couple of paragraphs. "The main battles in the areas of Central Bosnia Operative Zone will be fought over places included in this area. There are numerous reasons for this, but I will only mention the (main) ones. One extremely important special production industry, the command and the logistics of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone are located in this area, thus forming a separation zone between Zenica and Visoko, and the settled areas of Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, Bugojno and Travnik. The intentions of the potential aggressor are to take control of the local HVO and destroy it, as well as to link up with the border municipalities in the southern part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. "I believe that the aggressor will undertake direct offensive action against Busovaca and Vitez along the following axis of attack: Kacuni - Busovaca - Kaonik - Vitez, then Zenica - Kuber - Kaonik - Vitez, and Zenica - Preocica - Vitez." And so on and so forth. Did you receive this intelligence evaluation, this estimate, on this date?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the basis of what you learned later, did it prove essentially correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, especially the main -- the axis of attacks which were to follow in the Lasva River Valley and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 26th of March, you had a rather important meeting in Zenica. This was the next-to-last meeting between you and the 3rd Corps before the start of the conflict between the Croats and Muslims. Could you just first mention who was mentioned in this meeting? I know this is the end of the day. We'll see whether we'll be able to get through with the conclusions of this meeting. Well, we could then stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Today is Wednesday. We will start again tomorrow at 10.00. We will start tomorrow at quarter after ten tomorrow, quarter after ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.28 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of February, 1999, at 10.15 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
